title: Debug: Valid/Ready Register Slice
constraints: Intended behavior: a one-entry pipeline register between two valid/ready interfaces. A transfer happens on an edge where valid and ready are both 1.
`in_ready = !out_valid || out_ready`: the slot is free, or it is being emptied this cycle.
On each edge: if the input transfers, `out_data <= in_data` and `out_valid <= 1`. Otherwise, if the output transfers, `out_valid <= 0`. Synchronous reset clears `out_valid`.
`out_data` must not change while `out_valid && !out_ready` (data stays stable under backpressure). The starter has **2 bugs**.
hints: Hold `out_ready = 0` with `out_valid = 1`, then offer new input data. What happens to the held word?
Transfer on both sides in the same cycle (a steady stream). Does `out_valid` stay high?
Priority matters: loading a new word must win over emptying the slot.

examples.title: full throughput
examples.expected: one word per cycle, out_valid stays 1

examples.title: stall
examples.input: out_ready = 0 while new data is offered
